Definition: from a compound of G2095 and a derivative of the base of G5157 (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose); witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry:--jesting.
BiblicalUsage: eutrapelía is the word for jesting. In Ephesians 5:4, the text says "nor jesting."
TheologicalSignificance: In eutrapelía I find no hidden theology; it simply means jesting.
